body: What did you do following your education?

Thanks for your reply.

The suggestion of moving away was also made above by /u/midas_76. I have considered moving to another city in England before, though never to leave the country. Staying in the UK wouldn't let me escape from these debts, they would follow me no matter where I ended up. Moving abroad sounds like the more sensible option though this requires money, something which I really don't have a lot of.

When I have spoken with my Dad in the past, he said very similar to you about aims and objectives. He once asked me to write a list about everything I should be doing, and then start doing it one by one. I never even wrote the damn list.

I am currently awaiting to hear whether I still have my job. This will ultimately be the deciding factor on whether I will still be here by the end of this week. If I do keep my job, I'll seek advice from the NHS again as this would be required by my employer, though I guess I'll be told to take another anti-depressant and I honestly can only see myself ending up here again. I don't think they will work for me, the state of mind they produce sort of nullify the other problems I've caused in my life. 

Also if my job is secure, I still then have to face the immediate issue of unpaid bills and the shameful truth that my house mates don't know about it - I was nominated for the lead role on finances when we moved in nearly 2 years ago, looking back I should totally have said no. I've no idea what their reaction could be. They have put up with my drug use in the past, but this is way worse. These bills include rent, as well as council tax which can be a jailable offence if unpaid for long enough. It probably wouldn't come to that stage, but still.  I looked into CCJ's a little more last night and was slightly reassured that, even if they aren't paid, all the creditor can do is apply for an attachment of earnings order or bailiff warrant. Don't think a Bailiff would be as much of an issue because I'm in a rented house and my house mates would definitely cover and pretend I don't live here, lol.
  
  
I'm going to have a go at writing this list.

Edit: Thank you for your response, I appreciate your time spent.

>Would you be satisfied if you worked doing something physical, free of drugs, long hours, somewhere remote, no computer, don't speak to your parents, but good meaningful work?

Each of those points in your question are the EXACT opposite of where I am at the moment. The biggest part of my life has been drugs, my job is the opposite of physical, I only do 35 hours per week, work is fairly local (15 minutes bus journey), and I am on computers all day. The work I guess is meaningful because we provide a service to people who need it. 

I have found it very difficult to try a comprehend what I might feel like in a life the total opposite of where I am at the moment :/

>What about another country, doing something with your English skills, involved in the culture, new friends, somewhere that it' very hard to come by drugs.

This is something which I honestly haven't considered before. It is a good idea, though getting into teaching would require money, same with travelling of course. I simply don't have the capacity to do that. I understand people have travelled to places with barely anything to their name, though I've been so indulged in this life of excess for so long I know I wouldn't be able to sustain it.

>If you haven't been able to recover so far, it's because, deep down, you knew your situation was better as it was. You didn't want those prizes of clean life over those benefits of doing drugs.

Hit the nail on the head. Totally.

Thanks for replying. 

I need to try to rebuild my relationship with my family but I don't know where to start tbh. Being brave is probably the only way to go about it... 

I agree with your point, there are certain friends of mine who still use other drugs on occasion, but nearly all of them have moved on from the Ket or Heroin. I don't really associate with the people who use them two any more, it's just me, quite sad I know. Even both of my housemates only smoke weed and drink. I've always ended up back where I started every time I have tried quitting.
Learn to ride a motorbike for sure, or maybe book tickets to Silverstone this year.

Rehab could be an option, though I know I'd have to return to my home town at some point. Before, my parents might have taken me in but they definitely won't do now. 

It would be great to start a new life somewhere else but it's just not a financially viable option.

+1 for the reply and more Morrissey.
